function.mechanism: Provides sweetness with incomplete small-intestinal absorption and colonic fermentation; this contributes to lower glycaemic response and can produce laxative effects at higher doses.
common_food_categories: reduced-sugar foods using noncariogenic sweetener claims

adi.basis: EFSA sweeteners table lists E966 as re-evaluation ongoing; no completed EFSA ADI value for E966 is presented on that page.

efsa.key_finding: E966 (Lactitols) is listed as an authorized EU sweetener with EFSA re-evaluation ongoing (last reviewed date on page: 17 February 2026).

adi.basis: JECFA evaluation year 1983: ADI not specified.

concerns.summary: Dose-related gastrointestinal effects are documented, including diarrhea at higher bolus doses in human observations.
A 2026 case report described oxalate nephropathy and acute kidney injury after prolonged intake of a lactitol-containing supplement with persistent diarrhea.
A 2023 in vitro study in human lymphocytes did not find significant genotoxic effects at tested concentrations, though mitotic index was reduced at higher concentrations.

no_concern_confirmed: No lactitol entry identified in IARC Monographs classification dataset.
Recent in vitro genotoxicity paper did not show significant genotoxic signal at tested concentrations.

adi_exceedance.notes: Numeric ADI exceedance is not applicable because JECFA ADI is not specified; practical risk management is driven by gastrointestinal tolerance and high-intake misuse scenarios.

risk_assessment.rationale: Regulatory evidence supports low toxicological concern at intended food-use levels, while high-dose gastrointestinal effects and a rare severe case report argue against risk_free classification.
key_factors: EFSA status for E966 is re-evaluation ongoing while remaining authorized
eCFR includes lactitol in nutrition and dental-caries claim framework
Documented dose-related diarrhea/laxation at higher intakes
Single recent severe renal case report at prolonged high intake
